Analysis by Richard Cowan

On January 11th The Murdoch-owned London Times carried a story by David Rose under the headline: “500 cannabis smokers a week seek medical help since drug downgrading.”
See 

Classic Reefer Madness At London Times: "Woman who killed father 'driven mad by cannabis.'" Quacks and Hacks and Schizophrenia. Is It Paranoid to Distrust Politicized Science? 

It went on to say, “The number of people needing medical treatment as a result of cannabis use has risen by roughly half since the Government’s decision to downgrade the drug four years ago, figures have shown. 

Since cannabis was changed from a Class B to a Class C drug in 2004, the equivalent of nearly 500 adults and children have been treated every week for its effects. 

The Times reported this week that the decision is set to be reversed, with cannabis likely to revert to Class B status after an official review this spring. 

David Blunkett, the former Home Secretary, downgraded cannabis in January 2004, making possession a nonarrestable offence in most cases. 

Since then, more than 16,500 adults a year have attended hospital citing health problems caused by cannabis, hospital statistics show. In addition, the number of children needing medical attention after smoking the drug has risen to more than 9,200.” 

On the same day, the once great Telegraph carried a similar story by James Kirkup, and Richard Edwards under the headline “Abuse Of Cannabis Puts 500 A Week In Hospital”. 

It began by saying, “The public health impact of the Government's decision to downgrade cannabis is disclosed today in official figures showing a 50 per cent rise in the number of people requiring medical treatment after using the drug. 

Since cannabis was downgraded from a Class B to a Class C drug, the number of adults being treated in hospitals and clinics in England for its effects has risen to more than 16,500 a year. In addition, the number of children needing medical attention after smoking the drug has risen to more than 9,200.
 

Doctors say cannabis abuse can contribute to a series of mental health problems 

Almost 500 adults and children are treated in hospitals and clinics every week for the effects of cannabis.

Its health toll is revealed in official data compiled by health authorities and obtained by The Daily Telegraph.” 

First, it should be noted that cannabis use has actually declined since it was downgraded from B (amphetamines and barbiturates) to C (steroids and most benzodiazepines like Valium.) 

See 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for November 1, 2007 Fall In UK Use After “Decrim” Violates Prohibitionist Party Line; Democratic Candidates Not Too Democratic. Denver Voters To Defy Establishment? 

Second, logic text books site a common form of logical fallacy “post hoc ergo propter hoc, after that therefore because of that. Notice that both papers say that the reclassification caused the hospitalizations. “Thousands of people have been killed in Iraq since cannabis was downgraded!” 

The sad fact is that the UK’s newspapers, with a very few exceptions have betrayed the most basic principles of journalism, and even basic morality. 

See 

Dan Gardner of The Ottawa Citizen Continues Iconoclastic Practice of Questioning Government Statements And Checking Facts. Someday These Techniques May Even Be Taught In Journalism Schools. 

Notice that both of these reports cite public data, and give the impression that they have done real research to bring the shocking truth to their readers. 

Previously, I have documented a similar phenomenon in the US. Here the Drug Czar’s office or its subsidiaries have claimed that there has been an increase in hospitalizations caused by cannabis use. 

See 

Oh, Joy! New Lies From the Czar’s Little Helper, In The New York Times, Appropriately. 

and 

Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies. 

However, I am not as familiar with the UK system, so I decided to wait and see if anyone there would dig up the facts. 

The first to do so, not surprisingly, was The Guardian’s Ben Goldacre, who does their “Bad Science” column. 

On February 2nd he wrote, “There are no difficult ideas in this column. Like, for example,when I tell you about the Daily Telegraph front page headline which says "Abuse of cannabis puts 500 a week in hospital", and it turns out they're actually quoting a figure from a report on the number of people having contact with any drug treatment service of any variety.

The colossal majority of these, of course, are outpatient appointments for drugs counselling, not hospital admissions. So there are not 500 people a week suddenly being put into hospital by cannabis. But this is not a news story: like their recurring dodgy abortion figures, it is the venal moralising of a passing puritan, dressed up in posh numbers.” 

The second source was rather unexpected. The Independent, a center left “quality” paper – just as the Telegraph is a rightwing “quality” paper – in that neither is a “tabloid”, has taken upon itself to crusade for reclassification based on “their” discovery that “skunk” (what the Brits call sinsemilla), is supposedly so much more potent than cannabis used to be, and therefore more dangerous. 

See 

The Iron Law of Prohibition: Potent Pot, New Data and the Old Prohibitionist Party Line and Another Lie. 

and 

“Marijuana Isn’t Harmless.” Okay, But Why Isn’t It Sold Over the Counter? Or Would You Ban Something That Causes 300,000 ER Visits Every Year, And Kills A Child Every Month? (Trick Question) 

The Independent’s apparently independent Health Editor, Jeremy Laurance, wrote an excellent article today, “What Is The Truth About Skunk, And Have The Dangers Been Overstated? ” that debunks much of the current reefer madness, but also offers more insight into the lies told by the Times and the Telegraph. 

He asks, “Have the risks been overstated? 

Yes. A recent report, printed in several newspapers last month, suggested that 500 people a week were being admitted to hospital for treatment for the effects of cannabis - a 50 per cent increase since the drug was downgraded to Class C in 2004. The figure was repeated in reports this week. Drugscope said the figure, quoted by the Public Health minister Dawn Primarolo, was actually related to the number of people consulting community drug treatment services for help or advice where "treatment" may amount to no more than an informal chat. The actual figure for hospital admissions was 14 per week in 2006-07 - - and that was lower than the year before.” 

In other words, the number cited by the prohibitionist propagandist masquerading as journalists did not indicate that there was even a problem with cannabis and had nothing to do with hospitalizations, which had actually decreased. 

Finally, he concluded by point out that “Skunk is safer than alcohol and tobacco, which are legal and cause more than 100,000 deaths a year.” 

See 

The Strategy of Comparing Risks of Cannabis and Alcohol. When an Old Argument Catches On. Analysis by Richard Cowan
